lines_of_business: All lines of business unless noted in Program Exceptions
Medicare Advantage: LCD L38720 and LCA A58250 (First Coast) reviewed
sections_in_order: Position Statement (Great or Small Saphenous Veins; Accessory Saphenous Veins; Symptomatic Varicose Tributaries; Perforator Veins; Telangiectasia; Other)
Billing/Coding Information (CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, LOINC documentation table)
criteria_location: Position Statement only, pp.1-3 of 14. Criteria are split by anatomic target (great/small saphenous, accessory saphenous, tributaries, perforators, telangiectasia, Other). The CEAP key sits in a footnote below the position statement. Related documentation expectations are in the Billing/Coding LOINC paragraph (not in the Position Statement). Pages 5-14 are references and revision history.
procedures_covered: Ligation and stripping, endovenous radiofrequency, laser ablation, microfoam sclerotherapy and cyanoacrylate adhesive of great/small saphenous veins
Same modalities for accessory saphenous veins
Stab avulsion, hook phlebectomy, sclerotherapy, transilluminated powered phlebectomy for symptomatic tributaries
Perforator vein ligation/SEPS/RF/laser ablation (ulcer indication only)
Investigational: MOCA, cryoablation, CHIVA, non-microfoam sclerotherapy of truncal veins, ultrasound-guided sclerotherapy of tributaries

logic.top_level: pathways (one criteria block per vein type), each block an all-of with a nested any-of of 4 indications

k_of_n.quote: There is documentation of one or more of the following indications: 1. Ulceration ... OR 2. ... OR 3. ... OR 4. ...

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: No contraindication list. Exclusions are written as default-to-cosmetic or default-to-investigational sentences after each block ('that do not meet the criteria described above is considered cosmetic'), plus an 'Other' list of investigational techniques, plus one embedded negative in the perforator block: 'The venous insufficiency is not secondary to deep venous thromboembolism.'
logic.initial_vs_repeat: No repeat-procedure or retreatment rules. Sequencing rules instead: accessory vein needs 'great or small saphenous veins had been previously eliminated (at least 3 months)' or isolated incompetence; perforator needs superficial veins 'previously eliminated' and not concurrent. Reimbursement section limits 36471, 36476, 36479, 37765/37766 to once per leg (billing, not necessity).

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Persistent pain, swelling, itching, burning, or other symptoms are associated with saphenous reflux, AND the symptoms significantly interfere with activities of daily living, AND conservative management including compression therapy for at least 3 months has not improved the symptoms.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Indication 4 is itself an all-of (symptom AND ADL interference AND failed conservative care), nested inside the any-of of 4 indications; the flat bullet layout hides that. 'pain, swelling, itching, burning, or other symptoms' is an any-of with an open tail.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: The varicosities are at least 3 millimeters in size AND There is documentation of one or more of the following
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Fine as a conjunction, but the 3 mm applies to 'varicosities', not clearly to the refluxing saphenous vein itself.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: conservative management including compression therapy for at least 3 months
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'including' makes compression one example; is compression required or can other conservative care satisfy 3 months? Defined in the Description as elevation, graded compression, wound care.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Incompetence of the accessory saphenous vein is isolated, or the great or small saphenous veins had been previously eliminated (at least 3 months); AND
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: An inline OR inside an AND bullet; 'isolated' is not defined.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Concurrent treatment of the accessory saphenous veins along with the great or small saphenous veins meets the definition of medical necessity when criteria is met for each vein and there is documentation of anatomy showing that the accessory saphenous vein discharged directly into the common femoral vein.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Restates the accessory criteria for concurrent treatment but the accessory criterion 'GSV previously eliminated' cannot be true when treated concurrently, so the first bullet must be waived; the text does not say so.

extraction_hazards: Bullets render as a private-use glyph in pdftotext, so list items lose their AND/OR connectors visually; the AND/OR words sit at line ends.
A footnote asterisk on 'C2*' carries the CEAP class table, which lies below the Perforator/Other sections, not next to the criterion.

The bullet 'at least 3 millimeters in size AND' (no punctuation) runs straight into the list of indications; the same bullet is repeated verbatim in three blocks (copy-paste duplication), so a parser must not dedupe the three blocks.
Concurrent-treatment and cosmetic fall-through sentences are plain paragraphs between blocks and are easy to attach to the wrong block.
Definitions run together: 'Superficial veins ... two major superficial veins.Telangiectasia: ...' lost a line break.

Documentation requirements ('failure of at least 3 consecutive months of medical management') live under a LOINC Codes heading in the coding section, not the Position Statement; it says 'consecutive', which the criteria do not.

Navigation bar and the legal disclaimer repeat at page top; Revision history (Updates) is long and includes superseded positions (e.g. 01/15/20 'investigational position for cyanoacrylate adhesive maintained') that contradict the current text.
14 pages, of which about 9 are references.
interesting_structures: Pathways by anatomic target with nearly identical sub-criteria copy-pasted three times (saphenous, accessory, perforator), differing only in one or two bullets.
Default-deny sentence after each block: anything not meeting criteria is declared cosmetic, which turns a failed criterion into a benefit exclusion rather than a plain denial.

Sequencing across procedures: accessory needs saphenous eliminated 3 months earlier, perforator needs everything superficial eliminated, tributary treatment is allowed concurrently or after. The chart must show prior procedures and dates.

Modality list inside a block (surgery, RF, laser, microfoam, cyanoacrylate) is an any-of over procedures, not over patient facts; same criteria apply to each, so the checker must judge the patient against the block once, then check the requested CPT is in the any-of.
Other section: positive investigational list; MOCA, cryoablation, CHIVA and non-microfoam sclerotherapy never covered regardless of chart.
CEAP 2020 key includes C2r and C6r, so 'C2 or greater' hides a non-numeric ordering (C4a/b/c, C6r).

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = all/any/not expresses it cleanly ... 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: Closest to a clean tree of any in this set: an all-of with a single any-of of four indications, nested all-of inside indication 4. Strain comes from undefined terms (significantly, improved, demonstrated reflux), the prior-procedure sequencing and the procedure-to-block mapping, not from the logic shape.
